headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk: Prefect can pass workflow metadata into Rasa, which may treat it as conversational input without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Prefect can move workflow metadata through APIs and orchestration outputs, while Rasa ingests text/voice conversation inputs from messaging channels. A direct shared channel is not documented, but if Prefect-derived content is bridged into Rasa messages or files, Rasa could treat attacker-controlled text as dialogue. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Prefect output is copied into a Rasa channel payload or training/example text
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any Prefect output is forwarded to Rasa
Prefix all bridged content as untrusted metadata
Restrict Rasa intents to ignore workflow-metadata fields
Use a separate queue/topic for machine-generated content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad egress, while Rasa handles text and voice over allowlisted channels. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or direct file-content upload path, so leakage is not established. The main risk is limited to intentional bridging of data between the two systems.
conditions: IF workflow metadata is forwarded from Prefect into Rasa conversation logs
IF either agent is configured to relay shared artifacts into third-party channels
mitigations: Minimize fields forwarded from Prefect to Rasa
Mask identifiers before handoff
Disable logging of bridged payloads
Review allowlisted destinations for Rasa
requires-engineering: segregate storage for workflow and conversation data

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress and orchestration behavior, while Rasa supports multiple external messaging APIs but does not support multiple instances. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or mutable database, so direct write conflict is not evidenced. Any conflict would require an added shared mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend or queue
IF an operator routes both agents to the same conversation store
mitigations: Assign separate queues or topics
Use distinct service accounts
Lock shared resources before writes
Audit for overlapping destinations
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can generate workflow metadata that may be consumed downstream, and Rasa can turn incoming text into conversational actions across chat channels. If Prefect output is treated as authoritative input to Rasa, errors can cascade into incorrect replies or automated support actions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Prefect output is used as a source of truth for Rasa responses
IF Rasa is configured to act on machine-generated text without validation
mitigations: Require human review for machine-generated inputs
Add schema validation before Rasa consumes Prefect output
Log and sample-check downstream responses
Separate factual workflow data from conversational prompts
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only show generic workflow metadata, text, and voice data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The only plausible issue is if operators route regulated data through Rasa channels or Prefect workflows without policy controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through either agent
IF retention or residency policies differ in the deployment environment
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Block regulated fields from chat channels
Document retention settings for both systems
Review deployment region settings
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement at ingress
